title: Rigveda 1.39: To the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.39: To the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.39 is a hymn of 10 verses addressed to the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 27v-28r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.39.1-3 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 3, varga 18); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 27v
translation.original_text:
1pra yad i̱tthā pa̍rā̱vata̍ḥ śo̱cir na māna̱m asya̍tha | kasya̱ kratvā̍ maruta̱ḥ kasya̱ varpa̍sā̱ kaṁ yā̍tha̱ kaṁ ha̍ dhūtayaḥ ||
2sthi̱rā va̍ḥ sa̱ntv āyu̍dhā parā̱ṇude̍ vī̱ḻū u̱ta pra̍ti̱ṣkabhe̍ | yu̱ṣmāka̍m astu̱ tavi̍ṣī̱ panī̍yasī̱ mā martya̍sya mā̱yina̍ḥ ||
3parā̍ ha̱ yat sthi̱raṁ ha̱tha naro̍ va̱rtaya̍thā gu̱ru | vi yā̍thana va̱nina̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyā vy āśā̱ḥ parva̍tānām ||
translation.text:
1WHEN thus, like flame, from far away, Maruts, ye cast your measure forth, To whom go Ye, to whom, O shakers of the earth, moved by whose wisdom, whose design?
2Strong let your weapons be to drive away your foes, firm for resistance let them be. Yea, passing glorious must be your warrior might, not as a guileful mortal's strength.
3When what is strong ye overthrow, and whirl about each ponderous thing, Heroes, your course is through the forest trees of earth, and through the fissures of the rocks.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 27v (OPenn image 29, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.38.10 ‹-svanāt marutām viśvam ā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 28r, begins in RV 1.39.4 ‹dyavi na bhūmyām riśādasaḥ›. Verses 1.39.1-3 end on this page.

1pra | yat | itthā | parāvataḥ | śociḥ | na | mānam | asyatha | kasya | kratvā | marutaḥ | kasya | varpasā | kam | yātha | kam | ha | dhūtayaḥ
2sthirā | vaḥ | santu | āyudhā | parānude | vīḷu | uta | prati-skabhe | yuṣmākam | astu | taviṣī | panīyasī | mā | martyasya | māyinaḥ
3parā | ha | yat | sthiram | hatha | naraḥ | vartayatha | guru | vi | yāthana | vaninaḥ | pṛthivyāḥ | vi | āśāḥ | parvatānām

translation.original_ref: RV 1.39.4-10 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 3, varga 18); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 28r
translation.original_text:
4na̱hi va̱ḥ śatru̍r vivi̱de adhi̱ dyavi̱ na bhūmyā̍ṁ riśādasaḥ | yu̱ṣmāka̍m astu̱ tavi̍ṣī̱ tanā̍ yu̱jā rudrā̍so̱ nū ci̍d ā̱dhṛṣe̍ ||
5pra ve̍payanti̱ parva̍tā̱n vi vi̍ñcanti̱ vana̱spatī̍n | pro ā̍rata maruto du̱rmadā̍ iva̱ devā̍sa̱ḥ sarva̍yā vi̱śā ||
6upo̱ rathe̍ṣu̱ pṛṣa̍tīr ayugdhva̱m praṣṭi̍r vahati̱ rohi̍taḥ | ā vo̱ yāmā̍ya pṛthi̱vī ci̍d aśro̱d abī̍bhayanta̱ mānu̍ṣāḥ ||
7ā vo̍ ma̱kṣū tanā̍ya̱ kaṁ rudrā̱ avo̍ vṛṇīmahe | gantā̍ nū̱naṁ no 'va̍sā̱ yathā̍ pu̱retthā kaṇvā̍ya bi̱bhyuṣe̍ ||
8yu̱ṣmeṣi̍to maruto̱ martye̍ṣita̱ ā yo no̱ abhva̱ īṣa̍te | vi taṁ yu̍yota̱ śava̍sā̱ vy oja̍sā̱ vi yu̱ṣmākā̍bhir ū̱tibhi̍ḥ ||
9asā̍mi̱ hi pra̍yajyava̱ḥ kaṇva̍ṁ da̱da pra̍cetasaḥ | asā̍mibhir maruta̱ ā na̍ ū̱tibhi̱r gantā̍ vṛ̱ṣṭiṁ na vi̱dyuta̍ḥ ||
10asā̱my ojo̍ bibhṛthā sudāna̱vo 'sā̍mi dhūtaya̱ḥ śava̍ḥ | ṛ̱ṣi̱dviṣe̍ marutaḥ parima̱nyava̱ iṣu̱ṁ na sṛ̍jata̱ dviṣa̍m ||
translation.text:
4Consumers of your foes, no enemy of yours is found in heaven or on the earth: Ye Rudras, may the strength, held in this bond, be yours, to bid defiance even now.
5They make the mountains rock and reel, they rend the forest-kings apart. onward, ye Maruts, drive, like creatures drunk with wine, ye, Gods with all your company.
6Ye to your chariot have yoked the spotted deer: a red deer, as a leader, draws. Even the Earth herself listened as ye came near, and men were sorely terrified.
7O Rudras, quickly we desire your succour for this work of ours. Come to us with your aid as in the days of old, so now for frightened Kaṇva's sake.
8Should any monstrous foe, O Maruts, sent by you or sent by mortals threaten us, Tear ye him from us with your power and with your might, and with the succours that are yours.
9For ye, the worshipful and wise, have guarded Kaṇva perfectly. O Maruts, come to us with full protecting help, as lightning flashes seek the rain.
10Whole strength have ye, O Bounteous Ones; perfect, earth-shakers, is your might. Maruts, against the poet's wrathful enemy send ye an enemy like a dart.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 28r (OPenn image 29, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.39.4 ‹dyavi na bhūmyām riśādasaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 28v, begins in RV 1.40.1 ‹-brahmaṇaḥ pate deva-yantaḥ tvā›. Verses 1.39.4-10 end on this page; 1.39.4 begins on fol. 27v.
